summary:
Americans are voting today in the US midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's second term. Polls opened across the country, and results will start coming in from 6 p.m. ET in Kentucky and Indiana. On the eve of the vote, the Supreme Court refused to take up the Trump administration's emergency request to stop California counting more than 20,000 ballots, which the administration said included non-US citizens.

The United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday. US officials described the attacks as limited and defensive, according to CBS. Reports said the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles being used against US assets. President Trump signaled progress in negotiations to end the eight-month-old conflict, saying a deal 'could happen', and Vice-President JD Vance said he was optimistic about diplomatic efforts.

The death toll from a Russian strike on a humanitarian aid site in southern Ukraine rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, up from at least 26 reported earlier. Zelenskyy said Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, in a barrage that coincided with the US elections.

headlines.title: Americans vote in US midterm elections that decide Congress
headlines.summary: Polls opened across the United States on Tuesday for midterm elections that will determine which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's second term. Results in Kentucky and Indiana will start coming in from 6 p.m. ET.

headlines.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as talks continue
headlines.summary: The United States struck Qeshm Island, an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday, with US officials describing the attacks as limited and defensive. Trump signaled progress in negotiations to end the eight-month-old conflict.

headlines.title: Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site leaves 29 dead
headlines.summary: The death toll from a Russian attack on a humanitarian aid site in southern Ukraine rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, after earlier reports of at least 26 dead. Kyiv says at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village.

headlines.title: Supreme Court refuses to block counting of California ballots
headlines.summary: The Supreme Court declined to take up the Trump administration's emergency request to stop California counting more than 20,000 ballots, which the administration said included non-US citizens. The ruling came on the eve of the midterm elections.

headlines.title: North Korea denies role in $6.3bn Binance crypto hack
headlines.summary: North Korea denied any role in the record $6.3 billion Binance hack, which US agencies blamed on Pyongyang. Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's claims a 'provocation', and North Korea called the allegations 'absurd rhetoric'.

headlines.title: Israeli opposition meets as neither bloc wins Knesset majority
headlines.summary: Israel's opposition was due to meet Tuesday after last week's election, in which neither Gadi Eisenkot's bloc nor Benjamin Netanyahu's alliance won a Knesset majority. Party leaders will make competing cases to the president for who gets the first chance to form a coalition.

headlines.title: Asian Cup postponed until December 2027 over Saudi security concerns
headlines.summary: The men's Asian Cup, due to be hosted by Saudi Arabia, has been postponed until December 2027 because of security concerns in the host nation. The 24-team tournament will now run from December 23, 2027 to January 21, 2028.

headlines.title: Australia's social media ban faces High Court challenge from Reddit
headlines.summary: Reddit and a digital rights group argued in the High Court that the law restricting children under 16 from popular platforms infringes constitutional rights. Reddit argues the government's rush to pass the 2024 legislation produced an 'ill-thought-out' ban.
